gaps.sentence: You go ahead; I'll catch ___ with you later.
gaps.explanation: catch up (with) = reach the same point/level as somebody.

gaps.sentence: Please fill ___ this form and sign at the bottom.
gaps.explanation: fill in/out a form (British prefers in).

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ up all the milk — we need some for breakfast.
gaps.explanation: use up = finish the whole supply of something.

gaps.sentence: The company was ___ up by a larger rival last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Take over/take up a company' — here 'was taken up' = absorbed by a bigger firm.

gaps.sentence: It took all morning to sort ___ the garage.
gaps.explanation: sort out = organize/put in order, or solve (a problem).

gaps.sentence: The deal fell ___ at the last minute.
gaps.explanation: fall through = (a plan/deal) fail to happen.

gaps.sentence: He loves showing ___ his new car to the neighbours.
gaps.explanation: show off = try to impress people with your abilities/possessions.

gaps.sentence: The plane will drop ___ the parcels at the next farm.
gaps.explanation: drop off = deliver somebody/something; also become less (sales dropped off).
